title: Bioluminescent Tide Pool Post-Processing Lab
description: The user discovers an underwater tide pool scene where an iridescent abalone shell rests among translucent aquatic plants. Through a multi-step post-processing control panel, the user layers and fine-tunes bloom, chromatic aberration, depth of field, color grading, vignette, and film grain effects to transform the raw scene into a stylized bioluminescent underwater photograph.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with EffectComposer from three/addons. Load DiffuseTransmissionPlant.glb and place 3 instances at varying positions on a dark sandy plane to simulate aquatic vegetation. Load IridescenceAbalone.glb and place it centrally among the plants, slightly tilted. Use a PerspectiveCamera at a low angle looking slightly down, with OrbitControls limited to a tight radius to keep the composition framed. Add a dim ambient light (0x1a2a4a), a soft blue-green point light above the abalone, and a subtle warm rim light behind the plants. Build an EffectComposer pipeline with these passes in order: RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, ShaderPass for chromatic aberration (custom uniforms for offset strength), ShaderPass for color grading (exposure, saturation, tint hue via uniforms), BokehPass for depth of field, and a final ShaderPass combining vignette darkness and film grain intensity. Create a floating HTML/CSS control panel on the right side with labeled sliders for: (1) Bloom Threshold 0-1, (2) Bloom Strength 0-3, (3) Chromatic Aberration Offset 0-0.02, (4) Exposure 0.5-2.5, (5) Saturation 0-2, (6) Tint Hue shift 0-360 degrees, (7) Bokeh Focus distance matching scene depth, (8) Bokeh Aperture 0-0.1, (9) Vignette Darkness 0-2, (10) Film Grain Intensity 0-0.5. Each slider must update its corresponding uniform or pass parameter in real-time. Validate that bloom strength cannot exceed 2x threshold value — if it does, clamp and flash the slider red briefly. Add a 'Reset All' button and a 'Capture Preset' button that logs all current values to console. The abalone should slowly rotate on its Y axis. Animate a subtle caustic light pattern on the ground plane using a scrolling noise texture or procedural shader. Ensure all post-processing effects are visually distinguishable and combinable.
